author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Norway’s Princess Astrid died Friday at age 94, the Royal House announced. An older sister of the late King Harald, she made her final public appearance Wednesday at her brother’s funeral. The palace said flags would fly at half-staff from the Royal Palace balcony on the day of her death and again on the day of her funeral.

Astrid became Norway’s first lady at age 22 after the death of her mother, Crown Princess Märtha, in 1954. She served in that role for 14 years, assisting her father, King Olav V, at official dinners, state visits and public celebrations. She continued royal duties after Crown Princess Sonja assumed the first-lady role in 1968.

The princess represented Norway alongside three kings: her grandfather, father and brother. The Royal House highlighted her work on care and inclusion for vulnerable people and her long support for charitable organizations. She married Johan Martin Ferner in 1961 and had five children. Her death came two weeks after King Harald died at 89 following more than 35 years on the throne, closing an especially compressed period of loss for Norway’s royal family.
dek: The former first lady of Norway died two days after attending King Harald’s funeral and after a lifetime of royal service.
headline: Norway’s Princess Astrid dies at 94
